items.text: Iowa has no adult-use cannabis. Its medical cannabidiol program issues cards only to permanent Iowa residents 18 and over certified by a health care practitioner. A valid card from another state gives no defence in Iowa for a cannabis product that Iowa prohibits.

Hemp products: since a 2024 law (HF 2605), consumable hemp products may hold no more than 4 mg of total THC per serving and 10 mg per container, and only people 21 and over may buy or possess them. Selling or possessing hemp products above those limits is prohibited, including products bought in other states or online.

laws.rule: Since Senate File 22 of 2025, Iowa drivers may not use an electronic device (phone, tablet, gaming device) while driving, where use includes holding, viewing or manipulating it, unless the vehicle is at a complete stop off the travelled part of the road. Voice-activated or hands-free mode (single touch) and GPS are allowed, but not video calls, video streaming or reading messages. Police gave warnings only until 1 January 2026; since then they issue citations.
laws.penalty_signal: Simple misdemeanour with a scheduled fine of US$100 (about A$142 at A$1 = US$0.7040, RBA 30 Oct 2026), plus surcharge and court costs

laws.rule: Iowa state park guidance says hard liquor such as whisky and vodka must not be consumed in parks, recreation areas and forests. Keg beer is not permitted in campgrounds, on beaches, in parking areas or immediately adjacent to those areas.

In Iowa state parks and recreation areas, mushrooms, asparagus, nuts, fruits and berries may be collected unless signs prohibit it; other plants cannot be removed, and ginseng cannot be harvested in state parks or preserves.
In Iowa state parks fires are allowed only in designated areas or where fireplaces or fire rings are provided, and must be extinguished when leaving the campsite or picnic area.

In Iowa state parks privately owned animals must be confined or on a leash no longer than 6 feet (about 1.8 m); pets cannot be left unattended in campgrounds and animals are prohibited within designated beach areas.

Iowa state parks require registration with the person in charge before climbing or rappelling; the department lists some parks where these activities are not permitted at all. Check the individual park.
